issues.description: The problem statement and UML specify an Animal constructor with signature Animal(String, int) (i.e., name and age), but the solution's Animal class provides only Animal(String). This constructor parameter mismatch changes the required class API and will confuse students implementing the Animal class according to the specification.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the constructor signatures consistent. Either (A) update the solution and template to provide Animal(String, int) and propagate the age field to subclasses and constructors, or (B) modify the problem statement and UML to require only Animal(String). Prefer keeping the UML/spec and implement Animal(String, int) in the template and solution so students implement the two-parameter constructor as described.

issues.description: The UML and problem description declare an 'age' attribute for Animal (an int), but the solution's Animal class lacks this attribute entirely (it only stores name). This attribute mismatch alters the class structure students are expected to implement.
issues.suggestedFix: Align the Animal class with the specification: add a private int age attribute and corresponding getter/setter, and ensure constructors initialize both name and age (Animal(String, int)). Alternatively, if age is intentionally omitted, update the problem statement and UML to remove the age attribute to avoid confusion.

issues.description: The problem UML and description specify Animal with an age attribute and a constructor Animal(String, int), but the provided solution (and the template usage in Main.java) implement Animal with only a name and a constructor Animal(String). This mismatch in the Animal constructor signature and attributes creates a mapping confusion: students reading the UML may implement Animal(String, int) (and an age field) while tests and the provided solution expect a single-argument constructor and no age field, leading to compilation or test failures and extra cognitive load resolving the discrepancy.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the Animal constructor and attributes consistent across artifacts. Either: (A) Update the problem statement/UML to show Animal(String name) (remove the age attribute and the two-argument constructor), or (B) Update the template and solution to include a private int age field and a constructor public Animal(String name, int age) plus corresponding getter/setter. Prefer option (A) if the age field is not used elsewhere to avoid unnecessary complexity for students.
